summary: ObjectGenome has no declared total canonical recipe workload/cardinality budget. validateDenseArray() enforces density but no maximum size, so accepted recipes may contain arbitrarily many components, mechanisms, and affordances; accepted provenance/role strings are also not subject to a total-byte budget. inspect(), graph validation, canonical sorting/serialization, and recipeFingerprint() therefore perform work and allocate data proportional to caller-supplied accepted recipe size with no contract-level ceiling. This is distinct from the intentional chunked fingerprint support for strings longer than StableId's 512-byte semantic-part limit and from the active familyVersion bound in PR #296. Follow-up should define a versioned ObjectGenome recipe-complexity budget, reject over-budget recipes before expensive canonicalization/fingerprinting, add max/max+1 and aggregate-byte regression tests, and preserve fingerprints for existing in-budget recipes.
evidence: src/shared/Objects/ObjectGenome.luau: validateDenseArray() validates density only; no MAX_COMPONENTS, MAX_MECHANISMS, MAX_AFFORDANCES, total-byte budget, or equivalent recipe-work ceiling is declared.

src/shared/Objects/ObjectGenome.luau: inspect()/validateSupportGraph()/canonicalize()/recipeFingerprint() traverse, sort, serialize, and hash accepted recipe data, so workload and allocations scale with accepted recipe size.

Repository duplicate audit found no issue/PR/source invariant covering ObjectGenome total recipe cardinality/workload bounds; PR #129 intentionally added chunked digest support for long accepted strings, while PR #296 specifically bounds familyVersion.
Source-only capacity-mining finding: no benchmark, Roblox Studio run, exploit claim, or Hero Gate unlock evidence is asserted.
